text: In Confessions XI, Augustine argues that we do not measure a past event itself (which no longer exists) but rather the present ___ that the event has left in the mind — so that the mind, in measuring time, is really measuring itself.
explanation: The expected answer is impression (Augustine's affectio, the trace or modification a passing event leaves in the soul). Since the event is gone, what we actually measure is this present impression, which is why Augustine concludes 'it is in you, O mind of mine, that I measure time.' The measure of time is thus internal to the soul rather than a property of the external world.
